notes.title: Neurodeck 1.3 preview
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

We are happy to see that many of you enjoyed Neurodeck 1.2 and its features!

Update 1.3 is up ahead and after the changes brought by 1.2, let’s take a look at what 1.3 has to offer:


[h3]3 new phobias[/h3]

This means new faces, new attacks and new animations & sound effects!

There will be one Rank 1 phobia and 2 Rank 2 phobias – [b]a slight trigger warning for those who fear clowns[/b].

[b]Those new phobias are unlockable[/b], we'll explain this right after introducing those new terrifying faces that will bring up your greatest fears!

Let's welcome:

[h3]Cynophobia[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/3b7d0fd0af6a2cf7661434542298195712167ffc.gif[/img]

[h3]Gnomophobia[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/bcf761b54837ea9a91664ee38b4126174a011a71.gif[/img]

[h3]Coulrophobia[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/5df81bbcd041dc831aa7f0130acb927639f445d7.gif[/img]

[h3]Unlock system[/h3]

As you go through the game and beat mini-bosses and final bosses, [b]you’ll gradually unlock trials, Balcony cards and the 3 new phobias just revealed above[/b].

[b]This applies to new players only[/b], so if you've been playing Neurodeck for a while now, you will certainly have unlocked most of this stuff!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/f0b1201237cc424171ff5fcf3e35f2c5c3986680.png[/img]

[h3]New stories about Lei and Jupiter[/h3]

During your session, you're free to read these new stories that will tell more about their own phobias as well as why they’re using the Neurodeck.

Those stories will appear:
[list]
[*] Once you've beaten a phobia
[*] At the end of your session
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/bf7bf54ac5b51ab4a4f5257d3d6f2f7b4c7854c8.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/8ab420da15f9037e3ce0f26598c1a0d81a6ae762.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/fa8803955a72775f3c96bd95d4d5c6e11c77a56c.png[/img]

[h3]Bug Fixes and some little adjustments[/h3]

Such as text formatting for character’s memories when entering Gymnasium, living room...

Hotkeys for keyboard play will also be added!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/8c5c4ae0a39404d79c1c4324c88057912d55093d.gif[/img]

[h3]What’s next?[/h3]

After this update, there will be one and the last update that will focus on UX and UI, little adjustments and bug fix mainly. Then, Neurodeck will be stable enough to launch on Nintendo Switch! Thank you for your patience and your support towards the game!

notes.title: Neurodeck 1.2 is now live!
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Thank you for following the updates of Neurodeck! Gostique and Nemrod joined us last month to help with Neurodeck updates and did great work for this new patch. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1253860/announcements/detail/3041590589760012910]Victoria[/url] has also created new great art with a dozen new illustrations.

We added around 15 cards, a new preview system, new unique effects and globally new content that add a lot of replayability to the game. Next month will bring new phobias and we hope you’ll enjoy these new features as much as we do!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/e682517ae3864788a0efd5f3d82c1d9e5ec9b7f2.png[/img]
[i]Hospital Visit, Hiking & Drawing cards illustrations from the Balcony room made by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1253860/announcements/detail/3041590589760012910]Victoria Guareschi[/url].[/i]

[h3]Here are the features of this update:[/h3]

[h3]Balancing[/h3]

Some cards have been boosted, some phobias have been nerfed and boosted!

[h3]Damage preview system[/h3]

This new preview system gives you a better overview of the situation in-game as well as an additional piece of information. We hope it’ll help you to better understand the different game systems and that you’ll manage to make decisions in better conditions!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/ad3df63fa54b40d5ac5565bcb51e421ada42b4e0.png[/img]

[h3]14 more cards that belong to the "Balcony" room[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/af3c5cbb61f8c43dcc32df42d54bf721a8b2a699.png[/img]

Here are the cards that you can find inside:
[list]
[*] Acting
[*] Beach Nap
[*] Broken Mirror
[*] Couple Counseling
[*] Drawing
[*] EMDR
[*] Hiking
[*] Hospital Visit
[*] Masking
[*] Wheel of emotions
[*] Rorschach Test
[*] Snowy Day
[*] Therapist
[*] Workout
[/list]
[b]Those cards are inspired by psychology to strengthen the link to mental health[/b] (EMDR which is a sensory stimulation therapy, Plutchik's wheel of emotions describing the 8 basic emotions, the broken mirror referring to the syndrome related to psychological and emotional trauma, etc.).

It adds another room so gives more replayability and more possibilities to your strategy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/464bbc01d88d35dc223a4be11d3d52e6bfcb91e0.png[/img]
[i]Couple Counseling, Rorschach Test & Masking cards illustrations[/i]


[h3]New card effect "Discover"[/h3]

Inspired by [i]Hearthstone[/i], this effect allows you to discover a random card or can be a last-minute escape from a situation. [b]These apply to Balcony cards only[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/44541e6663c5fb88e14b5ecc8a5eb7bcf2228897.png[/img]

[h3]New modifier "Weakness"[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/e9b2e62d0e84148734784f0ef32734da54c128ec.png[/img]

Phobia or player will deal less damage and you have a preview of these damage on the cards. [b]This modifier is available in Balcony cards too[/b].


[h3]Player can gain Block[/h3]

Gaining Block will help you to build more defense and adds a little extra to your strategy. [b]You will find this feature in Balcony cards only[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/d381fc90535967e2fed1ae0614c4d87ea1225e49.png[/img]

[h3]New traits[/h3]

[b]Those traits are available in the Nursery room[/b]. At the beginning of the game, you'll have to choose one of three traits proposed that will follow you for the rest of your session. Here are the traits you will encounter:
[list]
[*] Lucky
[*] Tenacious
[*] Laid back
[*] Funny
[*] Messy
[*] Shy
[*] Honest
[*] Dare-devil
[*] Improviser
[*] Frugal
[*] Contemplative
[*] Calming
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/f9a7b6fe7c507c3686d85a6b11ce3e6ac349216c.png[/img]

[h3]Two additional resilience level[/h3]

In addition to the previous 1 to 5 resilience levels, levels 6 & 7 have been added.

[list]
[*] [b]Level 6[/b]: Nightmares: every phobia met is in nightmare mode.
[*] [b]Level 7[/b]: Mental Exhaustion: when you draw a card you lose 1 Sanity.
[/list]

[h3]New achievements[/h3]

Do you want to get more challenges in Neurodeck? With those new achievements, you’ll be able to make modifiers a strong weapon and to use resilience levels!

[list]
[*] [b]Resilient level X[/b]: Achieve a run with a resilient level. (1 à 7)
[*] [b]Passive-aggressive[/b]: Kill a phobia with a trait
[*] [b]Fast Forward[/b]: End a run with less than 10 cards in the deck.
[*] [b]Kill anxiety[/b]: Kill a phobia with the anxiety modifier
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/ed03b146076d4450d0c5f5c64ce8e7e53d52eb41.gif[/img]

[h3]Bugfixes[/h3]

Some bugs may have been added while others may have been fixed! It’s hard to track everything and provide a complete bug list...

[h3]Official game guide[/h3]

Check out this complete guide explaining a lot of game mechanics. Useful when blocked on a phobia or wondering about a specific mechanic. Feel free to ask for more details! A big thank you to Chloé for creating this complete guide.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2462195327

[h3]Modding in the beta branch for now[/h3]

Modding is WIP so locked in beta branch; still checking how it should be working for the best use. Thanks for waiting!

[b]Here is how to access Neurodeck beta:[/b]
[list]
[*] Right-click on Neurodeck app, then click on "Properties"
[*] Go to the "Betas" tab, then under "Select the Beta you want to opt into," select "beta - beta tests at your own risk"
[*] Finally, the Beta version will be uploaded automatically.
[/list]

[h3]Switch release reminder[/h3]

We're still planning to finish the updates in order to have a patched and finalized version for Nintendo Switch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/b4b6254455d3fea5fd30e18ee03db108d2ecb074.png[/img]

[h3]While waiting for Neurodeck 1.3, here's a little overview of Gnomophobia, which will be part of the new phobias![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/ea6708680f124d4de42afcb17cf6d202aa88cd67.gif[/img]
[i]Animation made by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1253860/announcements/detail/3044967655749991488]Jeanne Prigent[/url].[/i]

notes.title: Neurodeck upcoming updates & improvement goals
notes.content:
Dear Neurodeck players,

Thank you for participating in the launch of Neurodeck. The game had a good start until we realized the quality was not high enough and disappointed some of you! [b]We take this as a hint to keep working on it[/b]. Goblinz Studio & we have it in our DNA to not give up and provide updates to the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/b59d2b81981e03370234a0160be09ffa612c5953.png[/img]

That said, development is expensive and it’s hard to say when some issues are just non-solvable because they’re in the DNA of the game.

So, we have decided to make updates to the game for the next 3 months. We’re going to hire new people on the development side and reattribute tasks to people who can work on those updates. These are unplanned expenses for us [b]but we know it’s necessary for the game[/b]. We will try to improve some aspects such as pacing, content and game feel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/e8cb7ef9ca69e9d53253dbd45b27659d2097f12c.png[/img]

[h3]At the end of those 3 months, we’ll see what to do. [b]Please keep in mind these are objectives, not promises[/b].[/h3]

[h3]First priority: (hopes for the first month)[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Improving game pacing[/b] by adding tension with a boss and mini-boss
[*] [b]Completing bug fixing[/b]
[*] [b]Nightmare phobias[/b]: encountering a phobia the 2nd time makes it more powerful
[*] [b]Nursery Room[/b]: you start a run with new traits that will alter your session right from the start
[*] [b]Unlocking rework[/b]: you can unlock wayyy more content overall but by reusing the content already produced (cards, mental trials, etc.)
[*] [b]Improving Survey room[/b]
[/list]

[h3]Second priority: (hopes for the 2nd month)[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Adding new mini-stories[/b] here and there [b]to improve the link to the mental health theme[/b]
[*] [b]3 new rooms [/b]that will improve replayability
[*] [b]Improving card design[/b] and [b]making new unique effects[/b]
[*] [b]Improving UI / UX[/b] in several ways (more reactive, more ergonomic)
[*] [b]Adding new resilience levels[/b]
[*] [b]Adding new mental trials[/b]
[*] [b]Remaking the tutorial[/b]
[/list]

[h3]Third priority: (hopes for the 3rd month)[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]3 new phobias[/b]
[*] [b]15 new cards[/b] (not sure how they’ll be attributed yet)
[*] [b]Improving FX & game feel during fights[/b]
[/list]

notes.title: Big announcements for Goblinz 5th Anniversary!
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Today is a special day for Goblinz, as the studio is already celebrating its 5th anniversary!
For the past 5 years, we have been developing and publishing games we believe in. It's been quite an adventure, but this is just the beginning!

For the occasion, we have surprises for you including new games announcement and big sales on all our games!

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/goblinz_publishing/sale/publishersale][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33904811/031edc7df8b0e2ab9136d7024a38b2fa14a2f260.png[/img][/url]

[h1]New published games: Diluvian Winds & Defend the Rook[/h1]

We are so excited to announce the addition of [b]Diluvian Winds[/b] and[b] Defend the Rook[/b] in the Goblinz catalogue!

[b]Diluvian Winds[/b] is a [b]sail punk city builder[/b] developed by [b]Alambik Studio[/b].
In a context of exile due to the rising waters, survive as you expand your community in your lighthouse!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1561040/Diluvian_Winds/

Neurodeck has been an extraordinary adventure. We made a game about mental health in the context of a global pandemic that has affected billions of people. Making a game is always difficult and it’s even harder when we cannot see people since interacting is sometimes complicated.


Yet, the game is way more important. Many people don’t understand mental health, they confuse it with mental illness. They think Neurodeck will treat or ease their mental illness or their mental health. [b]It won’t.[/b] Others find value in having phobias and problems of everyday life displayed on-screen. [b]Those topics bring a lot of emotions and thoughts in-game[/b], that’s intended. Neurodeck is not a therapy. Go and see a therapist if you feel you need one, please.

notes.title: Sound design with Nicolas Gueguen
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/a0ab3c38bbe6180158fcb6efc03215d44aac2c77.png[/img]

[i]Nicolas is never out of ideas when recording sound effects for video games. His know-how and his endless imagination allow him to use turn his environment into all the sounds he wants on [url=https://www.fmod.com/]Fmod[/url].[/i]

[b][h3]What part of your job do you like the most?[/h3][/b]
Playing the game! And tweaking audio at the same time. Sometimes it’s hard to not get hooked and to stay focused on the audio.
 
[b][h3]Which sound effect was the craziest to record?[/h3][/b]
I recorded a sound that didn’t make it in the game. There’s a room called Kitchen and at the beginning, we were testing some audio ambiances to fit in each room. [b]I had to record myself cooking stuff, water boiling, pan-frying, cutting vegetables...[/b] Not very crazy but fun anyways.
 
[b][h3]Was it the first time you worked with voice actors? What did you learn from them and this experience?[/h3][/b]
I do a lot of vocal recording in my studio. So, this wasn’t my first time. But this time was a bit special because they didn’t have to say a word, just making onomatopeias. I learned that the key was to make them understand the context and the feeling of the character. My explanations had to be clear so they could perform this task with the game's intentions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/b937838d0260318cb4934037047206f91269b879.png[/img]
[i]Little story: for blenophobia sound effect, Nicolas used actual slime.[/i]

[b][h3]How hard is it to make sure that the sound effect you produce is the sound you want? How do you make your choices?[/h3][/b]
I start with a mental image of the sound, then I start experimenting. Sometimes, I just know where to search and things are coming quickly together. But sometimes, I just realize that it won't work, so just I start over. And when I know that I have great sounds in the right range in sound libraries, I go for them. It’s the more efficient method with often great results. If I cannot find a sound quickly, I go for recording, and I have to find a good-sounding prop. [b]If it still sucks, I just look for another good-sounding object, I change the mic positioning or go back to library searching![/b]
 
[b][h3]Is there a phobia or a card that reminds you of a special event in your life?[/h3][/b]
[b]Nails Chew[/b]! that’s me. As far as I remember, I’ve always bitten my nails. I tried a few times to stop, but it’s still there. People say it occurs when you’re stressed, maybe I am, but I don't feel like it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/0abc4e61252401ef698b1315135bdf574def8733.png[/img]

notes.title: Art direction with Victoria Guareschi
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/c90f1c641147999d16449138f19be43cf7f2d1a7.png[/img]

[i]Victoria is a freelance artist whose role was to give shape to Neurodeck's phobias, cards and UI. She worked hard to provide this colorful touch in this dark atmosphere when fighting phobias![/i]

[b][h3]How would you describe your job with your own words?[/h3][/b]
I like to think that my job is basically to give life to all those amazing ideas, concepts, stories that come my way.

[b][h3]What was the most challenging part of your work on Neurodeck?[/h3][/b]
Before Neurodeck, I had never worked on a deckbuilder card game before. It was really challenging for me to understand its features. [b]I spent a lot of time thinking about the interface and all of the elements I had to show on-screen while keeping the whole thing elegant and refined.[/b] Representing phobias was a bit challenging for me too since I had never drawn monstrous things like this before. [b]My usual style is more like the one you can see on card illustrations.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/0d50dba67a54252e3ea2e07472d7746a10d90563.png[/img]
[i]Some of Victoria's favorite card illustrations.[/i]

[b][h3]Did you find the mental health issue inspiring? Why?[/h3][/b]
Yes, I did. First off, because I’ve always felt the need to give sense to my work. Also, I have had mental health issues in my life, just like a lot of people, so [b]I just inspired myself with those feelings to be as fair as possible in my representations of it.[/b] 

[b][h3]What are your main and favorite tools?[/h3][/b]

I have two cats at home, and when I feel down or lonely during the day – since I work from home full time, – I love to just take a break and cuddle them for a moment. It always makes me feel a lot better. For this reason, the cat I drew on this card is a mix of my two beloved cats!

notes.title: Music composition with Tilia Weevers
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/abdfabd5da25dc6d13eeca45945650ce6e15e047.png[/img]

[i]Tilia has an amazing musical sensibility and has a very good adaptation capacity. She composed and played the music for Neurodeck.[/i]

[b][h3]How would you describe your job in your own words?[/h3][/b]
I do lots of things actually! I give individual singing lessons, I use my voice for voice-over, logo jingles or other stuff, I compose music and write songs, I make photomontages of fantasy creatures that I stick on canvas, I sculpt masks... [b]But the main thing that I do for a living is my singing lessons[/b].

[b][h3]How was composing for Neurodeck different from what you used to work on?[/h3][/b]
It was so interesting to work with the staff and exchange ideas and impressions with them for the atmosphere that the music had to give. I work alone most of the time, composing my own songs or instrumentals. For Neurodeck, [b]I worked with people and composed music for a game for the first time[/b], an old dream came true.

[b][h3]How would you sum up your collaboration with Nicolas Gueguen, sound designer for Neurodeck?[/h3][/b]
The collaboration with Nicolas was very intuitive, he asked me to split some of the tracks so he could adapt the music in the game. For example, he needed a "stressful" track with sounds on top of the other instruments for the parts where it was needed. The communication was clear and easy, I liked that very much.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/550b38b5ea0bf245b2bbce9af5c8e94b6ef9d1b8.png[/img]

[b][h3]Once you had an idea of what you wanted to do for Neurodeck, how did you come up with the composition?[/h3][/b]
I was inspired by the graphic atmosphere, the inner thoughts that someone can have when having to cope with different psychological phases, and [b]I played on my piano different themes that could be looped without sounding repetitive.[/b] I took great pleasure in working on this because I believe in introspection, I like searching inside of myself the emotions and making them "true" with music.

[b][h3]Which features do you take into consideration when composing for video games?[/h3][/b]
Naturally, [b]a video game is made by a creator, so you have to work with someone else's ideas.[/b] It requires a lot of exchanges and understanding with the people developing it.

During the development process, the music had to meet their demands, and [b]the composer have to adapt themselves permanently[/b], change things, and also infuse ideas here and there. It is a real back and forth!

[b][h3]Is there a phobia or a card that reminds you of a special event in your life?[/h3][/b]
[b]Nyctophobia [/b]reminds me of my childhood. I feared what lurked in the darkness, especially behind me. And one day, I decided to put myself in the dark and I turned around, and even if I could not see a lot, I felt better, [b]as I decided to face my fear, and the monster I imagined just disappeared[/b].

notes.title: Neurodeck tackling phobias and mental health is both refreshing and a concern
notes.content:
Bertie: It's the monsters that do it for me. They are manifestations of phobias, and even though I am lucky enough to not have any phobias (that I know of), they unsettle me. Take the Tokophobia monster: it's based around a fear of childbirth, and here it's depicted by a silhouetted pregnant woman on her knees, whose bulging stomach morphs into an angry child when it attacks. That's freaky, right?

Or there's the Haptophobia monster, which I think ought to be Haphephobia because it's based around a phobia of touching. Here, it's a creature made of many hands that all reach out and grab at you when it attacks, and it's grotesque.

There are others but I don't want to spoil them. But it's the way they're brought to life, the way they look and behave, moving as if made for a vintage cartoon, in a kind of flick-book animated way, which speaks to a kind of quality in Neurodeck which elevates it. That, hand-in-hand with the game's focus on mental health, and cards themed around ways to deal with phobias, and keeping a mind calm and positive, are what makes Neurodeck more than another game moulded around a Slay the Spire frame. They're its difference. And they manage a kind of relevance and connection with, certainly, me, that other games have to work much harder for.

notes.title: Game Design with Félix Moll
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/1e32c481756eb7ed898f9aaaf00402e1ac4b062b.png[/img]

[i]Félix is a passionate Game Designer specialized in balancing and ergonomics. He has freshly taken up his position at [url=https://goblinzstudio.com/]Globlinz Studio[/url]. He used his technical knowledge in roguelikes and deckbuilders for the development of Neurodeck as a freelance Game Designer.[/i]

[b][h3]What are the most important qualities for a Game Designer according to you?[/h3][/b]
In my opinion, the ability to [b]communicate efficiently[/b] with other team members is one of the most important qualities for a Game Designer.

[b]Video game creation is all about teamwork [/b], and communication is an aspect of the job that is extremely important in my opinion. Being [b]curious[/b] and [b]eager to learn[/b] are also important qualities because you will always learn new things while working on a game! 

[b][h3]What did Neurodeck teach you about mental health?[/h3][/b] 
Even if I was already a bit aware of these themes, I think working on Neurodeck helped me to understand how important mental health is these days, especially through feedback from players, playtesters and content creators.

[b]The game aims more to talk about mental health in a global way rather than describing a specific process[/b], which I find interesting as an art direction because I think it'll allow people to relate to this subject with their own words and feelings. I also learned a bit more about the phobias during the development, and it helped me to better understand how they can affect someone.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/13110840c1511521286faa46a263526ac2c5d15c.png[/img]

[b][h3]What are the main tools you use in general? Was it different for Neurodeck?[/h3][/b]
While developing content for Neurodeck, I used some tools of [b][url=https://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/167214/rational_design_the_core_of_.php]Rational Game Design[/url][/b] to create a distinct gameplay identity for each phobia and to differentiate the kind of challenges they gave to players. Concepts such as "set-up" and "pay-off" were used to create the structure of the main strategies of each character's emotion in order to maximize the importance of the player’s choices within the pools of cards. As a designer, [b]I’m specialized in balancing and making games ergonomic[/b]. I also brought methodologies from my previous experiences to work on these two subjects.

Another of my inspirations was Mark Rosewater's article [url=https://magic.wizards.com/en/articles/archive/making-magic/timmy-johnny-and-spike-2013-12-03][i]Timmy, Johnny, and Spike[/i][/url], in which he depicts three psychographic profiles of players identified by [i]Magic: the Gathering[/i]'s R&D. I think this kind of tools – such as Bartle's Taxonomy and Brainhex, for example – are great because they allow designers to consider what do different types of players like when designing a game experience.

[b][h3]What did you know about deckbuilders and roguelikes before starting to develop the game? Was there additional research you needed to do?[/h3][/b]
Prior to working on Neurodeck I gave a conference on the mechanic of "draft" and its use in card games, and worked on several roguelikes and deckbuilding games with the French publisher Goblinz Studio.

Before joining the team, [b]I also played and analyzed around a dozen deckbuilding games[/b]: I could better understand the specificities of Neurodeck, and how to design the experience using the strengths of the core gameplay. When I joined the team, [b]I also had the opportunity to play and analyze a few other games that were an influence for the team[/b] in my first weeks. Discussing these references and concepts helped me to better understand the creative inspirations of the game.

[b][h3]Is there a phobia or a card that reminds you of a special event in your life?[/h3][/b] 
I always had pets as a child and teenager, so [b]Favorite Pillow [/b]and [b]Dog Petting[/b] remind me of them when I play the game. I especially like the former illustration, because one of my cats was very fluffy and liked to roll over while petting him!

notes.title: Phobia animation with Jeanne Prigent
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/9b475f6d6ecd7b55a736c9f01fd310101a463cbf.png[/img]

[i]Jeanne is a talented and dynamic freelance 2D animator who worked on Neurodeck's phobia animation.[/i]

[b][h3]What is the part of your job that you like the most?[/h3][/b]
The part of my job I like the most might be making the [b]rough animations[/b]. That's the step of the workflow where you bring life to the character – for Neurodeck, they were phobias. That's the moment when you have to think about the [b]movements [/b]you'll make, the [b]personality of the subject[/b] and even [b]what the player might feel while watching it[/b]. It's the most interesting part of the process and I am thrilled everytime I start a new animation!


[b][h3]What have you learned from your experience on Neurodeck?[/h3][/b]
I graduated less than a year ago when I started animating for Neurodeck. I had already worked on games, but they were student games, game jam projects or serious games that weren't supposed to reach as many players as Neurodeck. Thanks to this experience, [b]I improved my animation skills [/b]since phobias' actions were movements I had never animated before – it was very different from the usual walk cycle, for example. Thanks to the team who trusted me and my work, [b]I gained a lot of self-confidence[/b] and I'm very grateful for this.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/fe32639babf939cd4093921da4303bd16a12decc.gif[/img]

[b][h3]How was your experience on Neurodeck different from what you used to do? Was animating 15 phobias challenging?[/h3][/b]
The biggest difference from what I used to do is that this time, [b]I was responsible for the animations only[/b] and had an Art Director and Creative Director to lead me. I had never been involved in a project which was at a fairly advanced stage either, and [b]I rarely animate characters that I haven't designed myself[/b].

Animating the 15 phobias wasn't too difficult. I found my own workflow I could repeat every time I'd begin working on a new one. They all share similar animations ([b]Appearance, Idle, Hit and Defeat[/b]) and then they have their own actions. Idle is the priority because every other animation has to start or end with the idle pose. During the process, I would ask for some feedback from the team, especially from my leads, to make sure this animation would match the design before cleaning and exporting it. It went well and I could even rework some animations I wasn't happy with.


[b][h3]Is there a phobia or a card that reminds you of a special event in your life?[/h3][/b]
When I worked on [b]Mysophobia and Nosophobia[/b], [b]I couldn't help myself but think about the current pandemic[/b]. Haptophobia as well. Those ones felt too real almost! Otherwise, even if I'm scared of spiders in real life, I feel like Agoraphobia is scarier than Arachnophobia for some reason.

notes.title: Narrative Design with Léonard Bertos
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/bcfd3fe1ca0aa19d09ad5af194e63a79caf829e3.png[/img]

[i]Léonard Bertos is a skilled and innovative Narrative Designer at [url=https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/goblinz_publishing?l=french]Globlinz Studio[/url]. He also took part in the Neurodeck development.[/i]


[b]What is the experience that definitely made you fall in love with your job?[/b]

I fell in love with the job before it was a job. This non-job was [b]modding games[/b]. It started with [i]Warcraft III[/i], which was more like playing Playmobils at that age, then I discovered how powerful it could get with [i]Starcraft[/i] and triggers and I made an infiltration game out of it. Years later, I released [i]Castel Uvirith[/i], a big – and strange – mod for [i]Morrowind[/i] and [i]les Chroniques Gargantuines[/i], an Age-of-Empire campaign about Gargantua.
	
I wasn’t even sure that writing for video games was an actual job back then. In fact, the position is still very new. The title itself is sometimes used to say either “game designer working with the writer” or “actually a writer with game design skills.” I’m more like the second one.



[b]What is the most challenging part of your job?[/b]

To me, designing is the most challenging part. In my job, I still prefer the “[b]game design first, then writing[/b]” process rather than the other way around because I feel like it gives me a solid basis to work with. But when I need to create a whole narration system that must be fairly cheap, save space, not break the gameplay flow, not need too much reading, can generate random quests and be translated into every possible language? Oh, boy.

Luckily, I keep in touch with other narrative designers if I get stuck. Turns out, sometimes, that what seems impossible to solve actually is. And you must make choices. Then, you must be able to work within this tight scope which can stimulate your creativity very much.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36907763/7f1c53978ba5542a4f9e5644fb59d810c6507540.jpg[/img]

[b]What has Neurodeck taught you about mental health?[/b]

Maybe the virtue of plain, explicit allegory? Tavrox had a specific vision of the effect he wanted to make on the player but he needed a hand on the achievement. I just helped the team to find a way to achieve it, mostly during brainstorming sessions. According to the players, it seems to work pretty well. Using “Hug” to get rid of “Something-phobia” takes part in an inner ritual.

I was already kind of convinced that catharsis was a real thing, including in video games. For instance, Doom has a splendid effect on my mood. Neurodeck only raises awareness on the process and approaches a lot of different fears.



[b]Did you sometimes feel like you lacked information about mental health?[/b]

I’m not sure but since we considered making a game much sharper about actual psychiatry and psychology than it turns out to be, and since I’m deeply convinced it works better as it is now, I guess I learned that mental health is not only about talking to a professional (therapist, priest or mom) but also using simple hygienic everyday helpers to face someone’s problems?

Clinging to day-to-day life to fight inner fears is particularly eloquent nowadays with the pandemic because we don’t have access to a huge part of our hobbies that help us to bear the difficulties of life.



[b]Is there a phobia or a card that reminds you of a special event in your life?[/b]

I guess [b]Tattoos[/b] is a good example. I used to be scared a lot about not having enough food, probably because of some childhood events and student poverty. [b]I ended up getting a venison tattoo[/b] on my belly, giving the impression that it was always full or as if I have always been able to fulfill my hunter-gatherer duty. [b]Gameplay[/b]

[list]
[*] This update introduces Neurodeck’s new character, “Jupiter”. She comes with a new “Inner Peace” mechanic that takes the place of Lei’s “Mind Focus”, a new “Meditate” keyword, and 34 new cards. As of now the character has only its first “Sadness” emotion available.
[*] Added a new phobia! Or two actually? Nyctophobia represents the fear of the dark, and Heliophobia represents the fear of intense light. The phobia alternates between these two phases in battle, and you will need to think strategically to defeat this powerful opponent!
[*] Added another new phobia : Nosophobia, the fear of diseases. This one constitutes another boss you can  encounter at the end of the Neurodeck maze, as well as Phasmo for example. We hope it will give players an interesting battle!
[*] You cannot encounter two phobias of the same kind (two “Arachno” for exemple) anymore. This is part of a small rework we are currently doing on encounters, more about that soon!
[/list]



[b]Balancing[/b]

[list]

[list]
[*] Fixed bugs occuring when Jupiter card effects were played.

notes.title: Update V.0.2.5
notes.content:
Update V.0.2.5 is here! It adds a lot of content : new cards, new illustrations, enemy animations, sound and music, balancing, bug fixing and much more.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/g8hrMhO.jpg[/img]

[b]What changed : [/b]

[b][h3]Gameplay[/h3][/b]
[b]Added a new “Meditation” room[/b] that allows you to unlock the traits/phobias/deck informations.
[b]Card pools are now differentiated between each emotion.[/b] Some cards are “neutral” (common to all emotions), and other are tied to one specific emotion
New “Collection” tab on the menu, where you can see all cards in the game. It’s still WIP, but it will give you an overview of the feature
A new “Mental Trials” tab has appeared on the main menu. It’s not active currently, but you will learn more about it soon
You can now equip traits directly after a survey

[b][h3]Cards[/h3][/b]
[b]Added new content for the “Joy” emotion of Lei. 13 new cards [/b]with a lot of unique effects have been added to the game! It should allow you to try a lot of different strategies
Two new base cards have been added to the “Joy” emotion of Lei
[b]The “Resentment”, “Inner Strength” and “Friends” cards now belong to the “Joy” card pool [/b](you can’t find them anymore with “Anger”)
Neutral pool : [b]added the “Psychology Book” equipment[/b] to the game
Neutral pool : [b]removed “Lullaby”  from the game[/b]. It might come back someday with another design, but we felt it was not an interesting option for players to pick
Neutral pool : [b]removed “Growth” [/b]for the same reason
Neutral pool : [b]removed “Anarchy”[/b], that will be reworked
Anger pool : [b]removed “Letting go”[/b] (might be replaced by something else in the future)
Anger pool : [b]reworked “Big Cleaning” [/b](new effect)
[b]Reworked Retrogaming, Alcohol [/b](neutral pool) [b]and Inner Strength [/b](Joy pool) to make them more simple

[b][h3]Balancing[/h3][/b]
[b]Nerfed Blennophobia.[/b] You can now fight it without risking nightmares
Nerfed Warm Tea, that now draws only two cards (down from three)
Nerfed the “Resourceful” trait, that now draws only two cards at the beginning of a fight (down from three)
Small nerf on the “Adventurous” trait (now gives 4 HP per trigger instead of 5)

[b][h3]Visual[/h3][/b]
[b]Added new illustrations for “Anger” : Comfy Bed, Kombucha, Flow, Spooning[/b]
[b]Added new illustrations for neutral cards : Broom, Pain Pill[/b]
Changed the “Self-Harm” card name to “Tattoos”. Added the correspondent illustration to the game.
Changed the “Therapy Session” card name to “Stressball”. Added the correspondent illustration to the game
[b]Added animations to the game : Arachnophobia, Herpetophobia, ToxicMascu and Entomophobia are now animated.[/b]
In game, HP and SAN heal is now animated

[b][h3]Audio[/h3][/b]
[b]Added menu, fight and exploration musics.[/b]
Added sound effects to Arachnophobia
Added sound effects to Blennophobia
[b]Added sound effects to fights[/b]: start of a turn, phobia attacks, playing cards and more
Added sound effects to the Gymnasium room
Added UI sounds

[b][h3]UX[/h3][/b]
[b]Discarded cards are now shown to the player.[/b]
Added screenshake on some elements
Added a visual effect that triggers when the player heals

[b][h3]Bug fixing[/h3][/b]
Fixed a bug occuring when a card was supposed to be played on discard
[b]Fixed a bug on the display of the tutorial.[/b]
Fixed a bug occuring on equipments that gave actions to the player (ex: Friends)
Fixed a bug that affected Gymnasium options
Fixed some bugs occuring when the new effects were triggered.
Fixed bugs tied to the new features
Fixed a problem on the “Deep Breath” card (created by some cards of “Joy”)
Fixed a problem with the “Nails Chew” card
Fixed sprite and animation bugs

[b][h3]Team [/h3][/b]
[b]Tilianna and Nicolas[/b] joined the team! They are working on [b]music and sound effects [/b]to give Neurodeck a distinct atmosphere. You can hear some of their works in the new version of the game!

[b][h3]What is planned for the upcoming weeks ? [/h3][/b]
We will progressively add new illustrations for the “Joy” emotion of Lei. It will replace the beta art currently present in the cards.
New phobias are coming! They will diversify the current pool and challenge players in different ways.
As we introduced a lot of cards at once, expect some balancing in the next weeks. Player feedback is very useful on this point, so feel free to tell us about your experience! 
New cards will be added to the “Anger” and “Neutral” pools.
New sound effects and musics will be integrated to the game, and will contribute to shape an unique atmosphere for Neurodeck.
New “stories” will be added to rooms and will help us integrate more narrative elements to the game.
The new “Mental Trials” game mode will be added to the game at some point. More about this later!

notes.title: Neurodeck : Update V.0.2.2
notes.content:
Hi folks, Update V.0.2.2 is now live ! 

You can get a key by joining the newsletter or Discord.
Check out : https://neurodeck-game.com/ for more details.

What changed : 

[h3][b]Gameplay[/b][/h3]

- Global balancing on phobias, with the intent of raising the difficulty by a little bit and to further differentiate the fights.
- Balancing on cards : we nerfed some that we felt were too powerful at this time, and buffed other cards that seemed underpowered. Special thanks to the players that answered our small survey on Discord!
- Added 4 cards : Resentment, Inner Strength, Kombucha and Grandpa’s Medal.
- Moved “Entomophobia” up in ranking : you will encounter this powerful foe later in your run.
- You can now equip passive abilities on the trait pannel in the exploration menu (it has a small book icon). “Meditation” rooms do not appear anymore in runs.

[h3][b]Team [/b][/h3]

- Jeanne has joined the team as a 2D animator! She will work in collaboration with Victoria in order to give life to the phobias that dwell in your mind and on the Neurodeck system. 

[h3][b]Bugs [/b][/h3]

- Fixed a few bugs tied to the application of buffs/debuffs on enemies.


[b]What is planned for the upcoming weeks ? [/b]

- We will focus on reshaping the second emotion of Jupiter (“Joy”). It will include new exclusive cards for this emotion, that will allow you to find new strategies to defeat phobias.
- Game difficulty is one of the subjects we are working on currently. We’re trying to find the right balance between “too easy” and “too hard” for the game, so there might be some changes in the next updates. Feedback are super useful on this, so feel free to tell us what you think of its current state!
- You will progressively see new animations be integrated in the game. Fights will be more dynamic and have different atmospheres depending on the specific phobias.
- New art for the cards is coming up ! Stay tuned :)

You can download the new build now in the beta branch on Steam. We would love to hear your feedback!

notes.title: Neurodeck v0.2.0
notes.content:
[h2]v0.2.0[/h2]

You can get a key by joining the newsletter or Discord.
Check out : [url=https://neurodeck-game.com/]https://neurodeck-game.com/[/url] for more details.

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]

[list]
[*] Added 2 new phobias with a new distinctive artwork : “Toxic Masculinity“ and “Mysophobia“. These should show up a bit before the end boss and offer a different kind of challenge.
[*] We made a global rework for all phobias included in the game (new attacks, new stats, new patterns).
[*] We also began a global rework of cards, traits and emotions in the game. This patch includes 10+ new cards for Jupiter’s “Anger” emotion and new effects that will allow you to try different strategies.
[*] Balancing on a few gameplay elements. It’s part of a global process we will continue working on in the next weeks.
[*] Panelodex => Cardodex + Traitodex + Phobiadex are now in game. Customize your deck & traits, inspect monsters. More gameplay freedom for a complete experience.
[/list]

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
[list]
[*] A new WIP background for game fights
[*] A complete rework of the Exploration UI, still in integration phase
[*] New character art for Lei, Jupiter is coming (we swapped them in the meantime)
[/list]

[h2]UI/UX[/h2]

[list]
[*]Global improvement of the quality of fights : these changes should improve the game feel and give players a better gameplay experience while fighting phobias.
[*]UI change for the exploration phase!
[/list]

[h2]Bugs [/h2]

Fixed a few problems that could occur during runs.

[h2]What is planned for the upcoming weeks ? [/h2]

[list]
[*]The rework of cards and balancing of elements (cards, monsters…) will continue in the next weeks. As of now a few things have been conceptualized, but it is important for us to integrate players feedback in our design process.
[*]A major change in gameplay is also coming in the next weeks, and should modify a few things in the way you build and balance your decks. You will be able to try new strategies more efficiently in a run, and approach card drops from a different perspective.
[*]We are also working on new rooms and another feature, that we will tell you about soon :)
[/list]

You can download the new build now in the beta branch on Steam. We would love to hear your feedback!
